comparator.name: Humanistic Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current programme page confirms a Dutch-language, full-time degree lasting three years, with 180 EC in total and 60 EC per year. The public 2026–2027 catalogue lists eight first-year courses worth 60 EC. The later years include an unnamed 7.5-EC course (code 0000), Psychology and Embodied Meaning entries assigned to different years, a 15-EC thesis and 30 EC of external study or electives alongside other third-year courses. The catalogue does not establish which entries apply to each entrant cohort or how the choices fit together. The 2025 accreditation report describes the earlier 10-EC thesis and 15-EC elective space and a planned curriculum revision. It does not establish the revised bachelor allocation. The verified first year is retained while the remaining requirements are clarified.

selectedProvisionalDescriptions.name: Personal & Professional Development
selectedProvisionalDescriptions.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

selectedProvisionalDescriptions.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. selectedProvisionalDescriptions.name: Governance of Sustainability
selectedProvisionalDescriptions.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
